turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come on back. You're the ankle, right. Have a seat up here.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah that's me. I can get up there, just, uh, slow. Twisted it yesterday.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sleeve up for me. Blood pressure first.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Sure. Practice was a mess, the field was soggy, my cleat stuck and I rolled it, and coach kept the drill going like nothing happened. Then Marcus scored and everybody just moved on.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mm. One eighteen over seventy two. Heart rate 76.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Nice. I run a ton so it's usually low. I'm seventeen, I play midfield, junior year. There's a game Saturday I am not trying to miss, Ridgeview's striker is like a tree.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Okay. Sit tight, doctor'll be in.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): What happened.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Twisted my left ankle. Yesterday. Soccer.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Swollen?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Puffy on the outside. My shoe barely fit this morning.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bearing weight?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I can. It hurts, but I walked in, four steps across your lobby, no hopping.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Where. Point.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Outer side, under the bump. Not really on the bone, more the soft part. Err, I think.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Numb?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bruising?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. Just fat and pink.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Not with this.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): The knee?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): It's not painful. Knee's good.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicine for it?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Two advil last night. Four hundred milligrams. Took the edge off. Trainer offered tramadol and I never took that, I don't even like how that sounds.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Daily meds?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Albuterol. My inhaler, two puffs when I need it. Asthma. Had it since I was like eight.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): How often.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm maybe twice a week, practice days. And I stopped monteleukast in March, that was ten milligrams at night. The lung guy said drop it.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): The bus smells like old gatorade by the way, which is disgusting, and somebody left a cleat in my bag, not even mine, so my history homework smells like feet now.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wheezing?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. After sprints. Not today.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest tight at night?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Looking now. Swelling over the outer left ankle. Pressing the back of the outer ankle bone.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): That's alright. Not bad.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Inner ankle bone.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope. Fine.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Navicular, top of the foot. Base of the fifth metatarsal.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Neither. Hey don't roll it, that part I feel.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ottawa rules. No bony tenderness at the malleoli, you took four steps, no tenderness at the navicular or the fifth metatarsal base. No x-ray unless this gets worse.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): So not broken? My cousin had a boot for months and missed prom, whole family group chat was unbearable.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): This is a sprain. Lateral ankle. I can't promise there isn't a tiny crack, but we're not getting an x-ray today.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I play Saturday though. I've been starting. Coach will be so mad if I sit, he already thinks I dog it on defense.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Rest it. Elevate it above your heart. Ice twenty minutes, a few times a day.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Ice is easy. Elevating in chem class is gonna be a whole scene but okay.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ibuprofen four hundred milligrams by mouth every eight hours, with food, next few days.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Same pills as last night. Alright. Do I gotta come back or what.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it's not better in ten days, or sooner if you can't walk on it. We'll x-ray then if we need to.

spec.situation: Young player who twisted the ankle yesterday; swelling, can bear weight with pain; doctor applies Ottawa rules aloud, no X-ray unless it worsens; rest and elevation advice.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Swelling present laterally, but onset 'this morning' isn't stated; only shoe barely fit this morning.
bad.text: Lateral ankle swelling (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, onset=this morning, temporality=current, body_site=lateral left ankle, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Weight bearing is supported, but it was reported by patient, not directly observed by doctor.
X-ray is conditional, but transcript says if worse and then if can't walk/not better in 10 days, not specifically 'worsening or inability to walk' only.
bad.text: Ankle x-ray (type=imaging, status=conditional, requested_by=doctor, indication=worsening or inability to walk)

omissions.text: Patient took ibuprofen/Advil 400 mg last night for the ankle and it took the edge off.
Patient specifically declined tramadol that the trainer offered and did not take it.
Left ankle pain location/detail: pain is on the outer side under the lateral malleolus, more in the soft tissue than on the bone.
Patient reported being able to bear weight/walk immediately and currently: walked in and took four steps across the lobby without hopping.
Negative finding: no night-time chest tightness was recorded, but respiratory symptom nuance was missed that wheezing is not present today and occurs only sometimes after sprints.
